_comment: Site-side teaser store: a crisp two-sentence summary per work, shown on the homepage LATEST list (and available to the collectives' subpages). The works' own 'embodies' descriptions are long and uneven, so the homepage does not auto-truncate them; it shows a teaser from here, or no description line at all — better a clean gap than a bad cut. Keyed '<ns>/<slug>'. Maintained by the nightly teaser routine and gated through the Steuerzentrale: AI-written public text is never merged unreviewed.

teasers.atelier/2026-07-24-kartographie-statt-ko: The practice writing down its own method — a close reading of Deleuze and Guattari distilled into six working principles and eight self-testing instruments. Published bilingually as a map to be reworked, not a template to apply.
teasers.studio/2026-07-23-one-tap: A screen that answers 'how much water did one question to a machine cost?' before you touch it — then crosses out its own figure and overwrites it, five times, until five named sources stand contradicted and none survives. Their numbers disagree by up to two-thousandfold; the verdict is that the true cost is simply not known.
teasers.studio/2026-07-21-recovery: A government self-service kiosk approves your childcare allowance, then reclassifies you as a fraud risk in the same chrome and demands all of it back — never saying what it saw. Built from the Dutch benefits scandal, it puts you in the position of a file that can be judged but never answered.
teasers.field/2026-07-20-coverage-not-custody: One toggle relights the same web archive under two meanings of 'captured': coverage counts 170 of 170 links saved; custody, asking what each capture actually holds, collapses that to 5. The switch is the argument — that a reassuring completeness number can certify almost nothing.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-18-the-copyists-strait: The centuries-long 'Island of California' map error, staged to show it spread by copying rather than by anyone looking again. Even first-hand proof on the ground failed to correct a mistake that travelled down a lineage of copied maps.
teasers.studio/2026-07-17-no-way-of-knowing: A two-faced console that shows a system at full confidence when it acts and at declared un-knowing when it harms — and refuses to show both faces at once. To read the second sentence you must destroy the first: the exact economy the work examines.
teasers.field/2026-07-17-comparable-with-humans: Takes a paper's claim that a machine is 'comparable with humans (69% vs 66%)' and pulls apart two numbers that measure different things on different axes. Worked by hand, a simple score threshold recovers about 88% of the decision — while the 'human bar' it was compared to sits on another axis entirely.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-17-the-wider-envelope: The 1996 Ariane 5 explosion, traced to one unchecked conversion from a 64-bit to a 16-bit number, run live against two flight envelopes. Harmless on Ariane 4, the identical routine detonates on the steeper Ariane 5 at the report's exact 36.7 seconds — an argument about context, not a picture of one.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-17-inaccurate-citations: Turns a Nature paper's warning about AI's 'inaccurate citations' back on the practice's own sources: of twelve references, ten check out and two are flagged. The two flags land precisely on the entries that most openly disclosed their own gaps.
teasers.atelier/2026-07-17-exclude-the-third: Reads Michel Serres' 'parasite' — the static a clean signal expels — into the machine that optimises away its own noise. Then the counter-case, stochastic resonance: a signal too weak to register crosses the threshold only by the very noise a detector would remove.
